newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa succession vote imminent, order says.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa succession vote imminent, order says.

text.p: The delayed election to find a successor to Mother Teresa at the head of her Roman Catholic order will be held within the next 10 days, a spokeswoman for the Missionaries of Charity said on Monday.

"The election process is on and is likely to be completed by end-February or early next month," the spokeswoman told Reuters in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta. "The deliberations will be completed soon. Please wait for another 10 days."

The election to find a successor to the ailing 86-year-old nun has been postponed twice since last September. The first election date of September 8 was postponed because the renowned missionary was ill.

The election by secret ballot was rescheduled for February 2 this year after a two-week retreat, but the electoral college of the religious order decided to hold another month of deliberations first and then the election.
"Mother Teresa is better and improving. She is attending prayers and participating in deliberations," the spokeswoman added.
A senior church official said the general chapter or the electoral college might decide to reorganise the administration of the religious order, which operates in 126 countries.
"There is a possibility of various delegations of power around the world to make it easier for whoever manages the order to function," the church official said.

"This is what is done by most of the big congegrations, which have a large number of members and who work in various parts of the world. It is quite possible that this model will also be introduced by the Missionaries of Charity," he said.
He ruled out the possibility of Mother Teresa being re-elected.
"I don't think the sisters will re-elect her and impose on her great responsibilities when she is weak, feeble and sick," he added.
The 1979 Nobel Peace Prize winner, affectinately known as "Mother", had wanted to step down in 1990, one year after she was fitted with a heart pacemaker, but was persuaded to stay on.
Mother Teresa has led the order from the start, shaping the mission's work with her strong, charismatic personality. But she now wants to retire because of heart, kidney and lung problems.
The election process involves the 103 members of the order's electoral order, or General Chapter. The college is comprised of representatives from various sections of the order's 4,500 nuns.
